gates.decides: Per-file line and branch coverage from an lcov tracefile, and whether each gate is at 100% of both
gates.impact: A gate with an unexecuted line or an untaken branch, with no record at all, or measured without branch coverage, passes

gates.decides: Whether test-gates.json and each allowance in it are well formed (reason required, no duplicates, no path in both lists, no unknown top-level key)
gates.impact: An allowance without a reason, a duplicated gate or a misspelt key is accepted, and every command works from a broken list

gates.decides: The defaults and the validation of settings: what a gate must not import, where its test is, which command is run
gates.impact: A typo in a setting silently falls back to a default, or a built-in rule is lost, and gates stop being checked for it

gates.decides: Where the test of a gate is, and whether a path is itself a test
gates.impact: check and mutation look at the wrong test, or a gate without a test is not noticed

gates.decides: Whether a path in test-gates.json is a plain path inside the package
gates.impact: A gate outside the package is accepted, and selfcheck writes to a file that is not the project's, and mutation names it to the tool that changes files

gates.decides: The name of the package, which decides what counts as an import of the package itself in allowlist mode
gates.impact: Imports of another package are taken for the project's own files and pass the allowlist

gates.decides: What counts as an object, a filled string and an integer when test-gates.json and a mutation report are read
gates.impact: An empty reason or a fractional occurrence is accepted as valid

equivalentMutants.reason: The value is an int there, and toInt() of an int is that int
The value is a double without a fraction there (it is equal to its truncation), so rounding gives the same int as toInt()

gates.decides: Allowlist mode: which libraries a gate may import, with which names, and which project files
gates.impact: A gate imports an SDK or a service file unnoticed and stops being a pure module

gates.decides: What a Dart file imports, exports and has as parts, which names it reads from the environment, which tests it skips, and where two blocks share a line
gates.impact: An impure import, a skipped test or a line whose branch entry hides an untested block is not seen by check

expectedTimeouts.reason: The loop over the tokens would run while the token is the end of the file. That token is its own successor, so the loop never ends for an empty file

gates.decides: The static rules for a gate and for its test: impure imports, parts, reads of the environment, coverage ignore comments, skipped tests, blocks sharing a line
gates.impact: A gate that does I/O, or whose coverage is switched off or whose test is skipped, passes check and reports 100%

gates.decides: How dart_mutant is fetched and started for the gates: where it is kept, which executable the environment names instead, which versions are supported, the plan and the arguments, which of its exit codes are judged by the report, and what is taken out of an earlier report first
gates.impact: A run of an unsupported version, of other files than the gates, or one that stopped early is judged as if it were the full run, or a report of an earlier run passes for this one

gates.decides: Which gates mutation runs again and which keep the results of the last run: what each gate depends on through its imports and those of its tests, what may affect every gate, and the record a run leaves
gates.impact: A gate keeps a Killed of the last run after a file it imports, a helper of its test, pubspec.lock or the SDK changed, so a mutant that survives now is not seen

expectedTimeouts.reason: Every import is followed again, also to a file that was seen: two files that import each other are followed forever
The number of directories grows instead of shrinking, so the loop over the directories above a test never ends

gates.decides: Whether a mutation run passes: which mutants count as detected, which survivors an allowance covers, when an allowance is stale or ambiguous, how many timeouts are tolerated, and that a part of a run is no result
gates.impact: A surviving mutant, a stale allowance or an unevaluated mutant passes silently and every project using test_gates loses its real guard

gates.decides: The probe that is appended to a gate, how it is removed again, and whether a negative control held on the line of the probe
gates.impact: A gate that measures nothing is reported as working, or a probe is left in a source file or cuts into it when removed

equivalentMutants.reason: How many bytes at the end of a file are searched for the probe. The probe has a fixed length of less than 200 bytes and is found from the end of the file, so it is inside the searched bytes either way and is found at the same place
The same number, one byte less: still more than twice the length of the probe

gates.decides: Which time zones the tests of the gates are run in, which names are names of zones, which command runs the tests, and which gates can depend on the zone at all
gates.impact: A gate that decides by the zone of the machine is left out of the run, or the run is made in a zone that finds nothing, and the mistake shows on another machine

gates.decides: Which command-line arguments belong to test_gates, which command they select, and what is handed to the test command
gates.impact: A typo in an option is silently ignored, or --force and --first are dropped and a weaker run is taken for the full one

expectedTimeouts.reason: With an empty body the index never advances, so parseArgs never returns for a command line with an option
The index moves back instead of forward after an argument was read, so the arguments are read again and again
After an option with a separate value the parser returns to the option itself and reads it again forever (the same mutant times out upstream)

candidates.decides: The shapes of a gate, an allowance and the settings
candidates.blocker: Data: classes with fields. The one thing it formats is how a violation is printed (file:line: message), which the tests of the commands read. Their use is covered by the gates that read them
A constant. A test keeps it equal to pubspec.yaml

candidates.decides: Which command runs, and the exit code for wrong usage and for an unusable test-gates.json
candidates.blocker: Imports dart:io (FileSystemException) and the commands, so it is not a pure module. The argument rules it uses are in args.dart, which is a gate

candidates.decides: The order of the steps of each command, what is printed, and the exit code
candidates.blocker: Read and write files and start processes. The decisions they print are taken in the gates; what is left is tested with stand-in commands in test/commands (for mutation: a stand-in for dart_mutant, and the tool itself where it is installed)

candidates.decides: How files are read, and how a process and its descendants are ended or handed a signal
candidates.blocker: dart:io throughout. Tested against real files and processes in test/commands
